rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not terminate a covered tenancy without just cause. Permitted at-fault reasons include nonpayment, uncured lease violations, nuisance, and illegal use. Permitted no-fault reasons include owner or family move-in, demolition or removal from the market, and a government order to vacate.

coverage_conditions.summary: Most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance, including buildings newer than October 1, 1978 and single-family dwellings. Applies once the tenant has lived in the unit six months or the original lease has expired, whichever comes first.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Tenant must have lived in the unit at least six months or the original lease must have expired, whichever is first. Units subject to the RSO are covered by that ordinance instead.

rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner's roommate, cooperatives under certain circumstances, some non-profit facilities for the homeless or short-term substance abuse treatment centers, and some properties owned by HACLA or the government.
rules.interaction: Applies to units not covered by the City's RSO. State AB 1482 may separately apply just-cause and rent-cap rules.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.

rules.title: Eviction for nonpayment only if arrears exceed Fair Market Rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may not evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent unless the amount owed is higher than the Fair Market Rent for the unit's bedroom size.
rules.key_value: Rent owed must exceed Fair Market Rent (FMR) for the unit's bedroom size

coverage_conditions.summary: All RSO and JCO rental units in the City of Los Angeles.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Applies to all RSO and JCO rental units.

rules.citation: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.quoted_span: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR).

rules.title: Statewide rent cap (AB 1482, California Tenant Protection Act of 2019)
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases on covered units are limited to 5% plus the regional percentage change in cost of living, or 10%, whichever is lower.

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential units in buildings older than 15 years, on a rolling basis, excluding affordability-restricted units, certain dormitories, an owner-occupied two-unit property, and qualifying single-family homes and condominiums.
coverage_conditions.owner_conditions: Single-family homes and condominiums are exempt only if not owned by a real estate trust, a corporation, or an LLC with at least one corporate member, and the landlord gave the tenant written notice of the exemption.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Excludes units restricted by deed or regulatory agreement to low or moderate-income households, and units already subject to the City of Los Angeles RSO. The single-family exemption does not apply where there is more than one dwelling unit on the lot or a second unit that cannot be sold separately.

rules.exemptions: Units constructed within the last 15 years (rolling); deed-restricted affordable units; certain dormitories; a two-unit property where the owner occupied the second unit for the entire tenancy; qualifying single-family homes and condominiums with written notice and non-corporate ownership; units subject to the City's RSO.
rules.interaction: The LA JCO does not regulate rent increases, so state AB 1482 may regulate them. Units already subject to the City's RSO are excluded.
